setup: Head, shoulders and back on the pad
Dumbbells over your chest, palms in
execution: Soft bend in the elbows; keep it fixed
Open your arms wide in an arc
Stop at a stretch, about chest level
Hug the weights back up over your chest
faults: Don't turn it into a press
Don't drop the weights too deep
Don't clank the dumbbells at the top

notes: Go lighter than for a press: the long lever loads the shoulder most at the bottom.
Keep the elbows slightly bent through the whole rep.
To finish, bring the dumbbells to your chest before sitting up or lowering them.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain that changes how you move

guideBrief.cameraNote: Side view at bench height, bench inclined about 30–45° with the head end up on the left. The near arm's arc must read clearly; the far arm mirrors it.

keyPositions.label: Top
keyPositions.describe: Sitting back on an incline bench, feet flat. Dumbbells held over the upper chest, palms facing each other, elbows softly bent.

keyPositions.label: Stretch
keyPositions.describe: Arms opened wide in an arc, dumbbells at about chest level beside the body, elbows still softly bent and pointing down and out. Chest stretched, shoulders still on the pad.

ikHints: Back and head stay on the pad
guideBrief.barPath: Each dumbbell travels in a wide arc out and down, then back up and in
